title: What this means for energy traders — Tuesday, October 27, 2026

sections.overall: The Iran conflict is still the main thread across all four markets. Last week brought a six-month Brent high above $116 (CNBC). Today's headline is about diplomacy: oil fell after reports that Iran's supreme leader and a top security official discussed conditions to end the war (CNBC). Headline risk is running in both directions, and the digest does not show which one is winning. I did not open full articles, so this note relies on digest headlines and summaries.
sections.CRUDE_OIL: Gulf exports have recovered to 24.6mn a day, above the 23.3mn prewar level, as ships use alternative routes (Financial Times). Even so, a fire near the Ras Tanura hub and Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities keep infrastructure risk in view (Rigzone). Markets usually weigh recovered flows against the chance of new attacks, so the two can pull prices in different directions.
sections.NATURAL_GAS: European gas hit a four-year high on winter supply fears (The Guardian). QatarEnergy has extended force majeure on Adriatic LNG deliveries to end-December (LNG Prime). Rystad says buyers are spending more for less volume, shifting toward spot (LNG Prime). On the supply side, EQT's deal for Range Resources would create the largest US gas producer (Financial Times). The EU agency's demand outlook, on par with last winter, depends on storage and LNG imports (Carbon Pulse).
sections.REFINED_PRODUCTS: Diesel remains the pressure point. Three Russian diesel tankers are heading to the US under a deal that has drawn congressional scrutiny, two of them sanctioned (Financial Times). EU diesel and jet supplies are tight, though the Commission sees no physical shortage (Rigzone). Indian export growth is expected next year, which is outside the near-term window (Rigzone).
sections.CARBON_CREDITS: EU carbon prices rose on colder weather and higher energy prices (Carbon Pulse). BofA has flagged winter upside risk to EUAs tied to the energy shock (Carbon Herald); that is one bank's view. The Netherlands says the EU will not renegotiate CBAM (Asianet). In voluntary markets, Verra moved the effective date of VCS Version 5 (Verra).
